rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The moderate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Raise temperature by 5 °C while holding the gradient fixed to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity improves the sole critical pair. The current elution window leaves ample room below the 10-minute time-penalty threshold.

Return to the better temperature and use a shallower gradient to test whether the critical cluster gains selectivity and resolution. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, leaving room to improve resolution without a time penalty.

Narrow the gradient span to reduce its slope and seek the small resolution gain needed for the critical pair. Raising the starting organic fraction should help offset the longer retention associated with the shallower slope, targeting full resolution before 10 minutes.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope while retaining the faster starting composition from injection 4. This should lift the critical pair above R = 1.5 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes, targeting CRF 1.0.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; now raise the starting organic fraction one step to shorten elution while seeking to preserve full resolution. Monitor both the critical middle pair and the early peaks for loss of separation.

Test whether higher temperature separates the critical compounds after their apparent near-crossing at 45 °C, potentially yielding a faster fully resolved method. Injection 5 remains the maximum-score fallback; this run also checks for new critical pairs as selectivity changes.

Slightly flatten the gradient at 55 °C to seek the small improvement needed for the new critical pair at R = 1.47. Check that the neighboring R = 1.60 pair retains full resolution while targeting a substantially faster maximum-score method than injection 5.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to seek faster elution than injection 8 while retaining its maximum CRF. Monitor both marginally resolved pairs, since the altered gradient window may change their selectivity.

Test a shorter gradient with a lower starting organic fraction to counter the selectivity loss seen when phi0 increased. This targets faster elution than injection 8 while checking whether both critical pairs remain fully resolved.

Increase the endpoint by one grid step to test the faster-elution boundary around injection 10. Its two critical pairs have little resolution margin, so retain injection 10 as the faster fully resolved fallback if this steeper gradient loses full credit.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with a shorter gradient, since the 55 °C region is now bounded by two marginal pairs. This tests a distinct route to faster full resolution while preserving injection 10 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a faster high-temperature regime where the troublesome middle pair may separate again after an elution-order reversal. This exploratory run targets a shorter fully resolved method; injection 10 remains the confirmed maximum-score fallback.

Shorten the gradient to test whether the apparent selectivity reversal at 60 °C opens the remaining critical pair. Monitor the neighboring R = 1.62 pair closely, since further compression may trade one bottleneck for another.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves the reversed critical pair at 60 °C, with a longer gradient to protect neighboring separations. Watch the first two peaks closely for compression; injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test an intermediate temperature with a fast gradient to seek a better balance between the competing middle-pair separations. The 60 °C trials introduced multiple bottlenecks; this run explores a different selectivity regime while retaining the confirmed CRF 1.0 methods.

Test whether a much steeper gradient shifts the middle-cluster selectivity enough to resolve the near-crossing seen at 45 °C. This is an exploratory fast-method trial; injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score fallback.

Test a modest temperature reduction from injection 1 to open its critical pair without the extensive crowding observed at 30 °C. This targets another fully resolved method below 10 minutes, with particular attention to the neighboring middle-cluster separation.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving injection 10’s slope and temperature. Because its last peak eluted before this gradient would end at the outlet, this should retain full resolution and CRF 1.0 while avoiding an unnecessary high-organic ramp.

Refine between injections 7 and 8 with a gradient slope of 0.065 organic fraction per minute. This targets full resolution near a 7.7-minute last peak, potentially providing more balanced critical-pair margins than the faster but marginal injection 10.

Refine injection 9 with a shallower gradient to restore its critical separation while preserving the favorable margin of the other middle pair. This targets a maximum-score alternative with stronger resolution margins, while retaining injection 10 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Lower the endpoint one step from injection 21 to lift its remaining critical pair above R = 1.5. The last peak is expected near 9.1 minutes, targeting maximum CRF with larger resolution margins than the faster confirmed methods.

Use a slightly steeper slope than injection 22 to shorten retention while preserving its full-resolution margin. This grid combination lies between the slopes of injections 21 and 22 and should keep the critical pair above R = 1.5.

Test a slightly shallower gradient around the fastest fully resolved method to assess whether its narrow R = 1.52 margin can be improved without losing full resolution elsewhere. The expected last peak remains comfortably below 10 minutes; injection 10 remains the faster maximum-score fallback.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower slope than injection 8, seeking balanced critical-pair margins while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, and the campaign has already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.0.
